- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 3–8% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates the drop; adjust forecast downward by 1–4% to match sentiment-driven mean reversion.
- Model tends to lag in early days of a new trend (e.g., after sentiment shift); for first 3–5 days of a new trend, add 1–3% to forecast to account for lag.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often averages out; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 5–7 days to anchor forecast, avoiding over-smoothing.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates near-term (first 10 days) and underestimates long-term (last 10 days); apply asymmetric correction: +1–3% for first 10 days, -1–4% for last 10 days.
